You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import numpy as np
A=np.array(di); B=np.array(do)
# hypothesis: solid monochrome rectangles get recolored to 4. Find connected comps of constant color in A.
from collections import deque
seen=np.zeros_like(A,bool); rects=[]
for r in range(30):
    for c in range(30):
        if seen[r,c] or A[r,c]==0: continue
        col=A[r,c]; q=deque([(r,c)]); seen[r,c]=True; cells=[]
        while q:
            y,x=q.popleft(); cells.append((y,x))
            for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                ny,nx=y+dy,x+dx
                if 0<=ny<30 and 0<=nx<30 and not seen[ny,nx] and A[ny,nx]==col:
                    seen[ny,nx]=True; q.append((ny,nx))
        ys=[y for y,_ in cells]; xs=[x for _,x in cells]
        h=max(ys)-min(ys)+1; w=max(xs)-min(xs)+1
        rect_h=(len(ys)==h) and len(set(xs))==w if False else None
        is_rect = max(len(ys))==max(ys)-min(ys)+1 and len(set(xs))==max(xs)-min(xs)+1 and len(cells)==h*w
        changed=all(B[y,x]!=A[y,x] for y,x in cells)
        print(col,len(cells),'shape',(max(ys)-min(ys)+1,max(xs)-min(xs)+1),'rect',is_rect,'changed',changed)

steps.text:
My enumeration was garbage (nested loops bug). Let me think directly about the rule from summary: recolor two maximal solid rectangles (color 6 area 45? and color 8 area 42) to color 4. Actually changed cells: rows 2-6 cols 5-13 for color 6, rows 16-21 cols 13-19 for color 8. So rule: find two specific large solid rectangles of different colors... Hmm. Which criterion picks those? Maybe rectangles with largest area among solid rects not contained in larger ones? Color 6 at rows2-6 cols5-13 area 5×9=45; color 8 rows16-21 cols13-19 area 6×7=42. Are these the two largest solid rectangles in input? Other candidates might be big too. Best: enumerate properly with numpy per-color components bounding boxes.

Let me fix the loop: for each top-left, compute max h and w such that all cells equal color — that's one candidate rect per top-left anchored, keep those not contained in any other same-color rect... but many overlapping rects exist within a solid region (e.g., sub-rects of a bigger solid block). For a full solid rectangle region, only its bounding box is "maximal by inclusion". Simplest approach: for each color, find connected component bounding box if fully filled; check solid. Then pick the two largest areas and recolor to 4. Verify on demo.

The diff set confirms exactly two regions get recolored to 4. My earlier cell had a broken enumeration; let me redo it cleanly: per color, take the bounding-box-of-maximal solid run.

G=load(); print(sorted(G))
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter
def comps(M):
    M=np.array(M); H,W=M.shape; seen=np.zeros_like(M,bool); out=[]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if seen[r,c]: continue
            stack=[(r,c)]; seen[r,c]=True; cells=[]
            while stack:
                rr,cc2=stack.pop(); cells.append((rr,cc2))
                for dr,dc in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    nr,nc=rr+dr,cc2+dc
                    if 0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W and not seen[nr,nc] and M[nr,nc]==M[r,c]:
                        seen[nr,nc]=True; stack.append((nr,nc))
            out.append(cells)
    return out
for k in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2']:
    a=np.array(G[k+' input']); o=np.array(G[k+' output'])
    ch=(np.array(a)!=o)&(o==4)  # which input cells became 4 in output
    tot=ch.sum()
    big=[c for c in comps(a) if len(c)>=9]
    print(k,'changed cells:',tot)
    info=[]
    for c in big:
        cnt=Counter(int(a[x]) for x in c); maj=max(cnt,key=cnt.get)
        rs=[p[0] for p in c]; cs=[p[1] for p in c]
        r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)
        n_inside_maj=sum(1 for r in range(r0,r1+1) for cc_ in range(c0,c1+1) if int(a[r,cc_])==maj and (r,c_)!=None)
        inside_all={(r,cc_) for r in range(r0,r1+1) for cc_ in range(c0,c1+1)}
        n_ch_inbox=int(ch[inside_all].sum())
        n_maj_inbox=n_inside_maj
        print('  comp size',len(c),'maj',maj,'bbox',r1-r0+1,c1-c0+1,'maj_in_bbox',n_maj_inbox,'bbox_area',(r1-r0+1)*(c1-c0+1),'changed_in_bbox',n_ch_inbox, 'ALL_CHANGED_INBOX' if n_ch_inbox==n_maj_inbox else 'MISMATCH')

def maximal_mono_rects(g,minh=2,minw=2):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); out=[]
    for r1 in range(H):
        for c1 in range(W):
            c=g[r1][c1]
            hh=1
            while r1+hh<H and g[r1+hh][c1]==c: hh+=1
            if hh<minh: continue
            ww=1
            while c1+ww<W and all(g[r1+i][c1+ww]==c for i in range(hh)): ww+=1
            if ww<minw: continue
            ext_up = r1>0 and any(g[r1-1][j]==c for j in range(c1,c1+ww))
            ext_dn = r1+hh<H and any(g[r1+hh][j]==c for j in range(c1,c1+ww))
            ext_lf = c1>0 and any(g[i][c1-1]==c for i in range(r1,r1+hh))
            ext_rt = c1+ww<W and any(g[i][c1+ww]==c for i in range(r1,r1+hh))
            if not(ext_up|ext_dn|ext_lf|ext_rt):
                out.append((r1,c1,hh,ww,c))
    return out
def f(g):
    res=[row[:] for row in g]
    for r,c,h,w,col in maximal_mono_rects(g):
        for i in range(r,r+h):
            for j in range(c,c+w): res[i][j]=4
    return res
for n in [1,2]:

    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}

        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])

        if all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rr):

            while r+h+1<H and all(g[r+h+1][j]==col for j in range(c,c+w+1)): h+=1

    G={}

        for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
            k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m)[3] if False else int(m.group(3))
            rr=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
            if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rr):
                G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rr]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))

def solve(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=collections.Counter(x for row in g for x in row)
    bg=max(cnt,key=cnt.get)
    seeds=[(r,c,g[r][c]) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if cnt[g[r][c]]==1]
    out=[]
    for r in range(H):
        row=[]
        for c in range(W):
            ds=sorted((max(abs(r-sr),abs(c-sc)),col,sr,sc) for sr,sc,col in seeds)

            winners=[col for d,col,sr,sc in ds if d==dmin]
            col=winners[0] if len(winners)==1 else bg
